newsitem.title: EGYPT: Red Army guerrillas to be tried in Lebanon - PM.
newsitem.headline: Red Army guerrillas to be tried in Lebanon - PM.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said on Thursday that alleged Red Army guerrillas arrested in Beirut last month would be tried and would serve their sentences in Lebanon.
"The Japanese government confirmed to us that those Japanese were from the Red Army," Hariri told reporters after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.

"They violated the Lebanese law...and consequently they will be tried (in Lebanon), and if they are sentenced, they will serve the sentences in Lebanon and after that we will take a decision," he added.
Lebanese authorities charged the five with passport forgery and other offences carrying up to 10 years in jail.
One of them told a Lebanese paper they would commit suicide in jail if Lebanon decided to hand them over to Japan.
Lebanon and Japan do not have an extradition agreement.
